commits.summary: Merge the four foundations streams: heap, summaries, observations and alignment
commits.body:
The reconcile of llm-dlc/loops/foundations.md. All four streams had stopped with Status: done and nothing deferred by the timebox. Each stream's last turns were recorded on its branch, their logs copied here, and the four branches merged with the default line. The workspaces heap, summaries, observations, alignment and integration were forgotten; their directories stay on disk for the user to delete.

Conflicts resolved: equivalence.rs (heap's object inputs, correspondence and identity comparisons against summaries' proof cache, proved helpers and per-callee refinement; summaries' replay_on now carries heap's comparisons), main.rs, examples/tools/build.py, lib/README.md, and the generated examples router (rebuilt with build.py --index-only) and trace files.

The integration check never ran a test on the combined streams, because every merge from 05:01 on conflicted. The merge found one real disagreement between streams: heap's Domain.may_alias was skipped when empty but had no serde default, so once summaries made Statement deserializable, no result could be stored in the proof cache, and compositional reuse of shop.Pricing#discount in shop.Pricing#total failed. It is fixed with the default.

Other fixes: shared-IR additions threaded through (Outcome.problem filled in effects.rs and the cache's records; Counterexample.differs and .jvm stored by the cache); a proved helper's own check no longer inherits its caller's --correspondence, --nullable and --may-alias; and the canonical claim names those three options outright.

Verified inline: the integration contract (lib/tests/foundations.rs) gives 24 passed, 0 unsupported, 0 failed. The whole Rust suite passes (unit tests and every integration test binary, the conformance cases on a real java among them), and so does every Python suite (verification, llm-dlc/tools, examples/tools, lib/solvers, lib/benchmark).

The brief's Progress folds the streams' work and lists the 21 jobs they left pending for review. One job came back during the run: heap's H1 benchmark, which failed (VF-014). The next step is Phase 5.

Out of date in the rest of the brief: 'Where it starts from' describes the code before the streams ran. Shared-callee refinement is no longer all or nothing (summaries S5), and objects, nullability and aliasing among inputs are now supported (heap H1-H4).

commits.summary: Foundations Progress: name the streams' commits by change id
commits.body: The merge commit's Progress cited the streams' commits by commit id, but sync.py rewrites commit ids when it adds trace lines to earlier commits, and the merge's own trace commit had already done so. Every commit Progress cites is now named by its change id, which stays put, and Progress says why. Checked by resolving each id with jj log.

commits.summary: Phase 5's joint run: jvmcontract compare, the four parts fed by each other on the joint example, every row checked but exact reuse at the entry points
commits.body:
jvmcontract compare BEFORE AFTER [--cache DIR] (lib/src/compare.rs) runs the foundations loop's four parts together with nothing written by hand. The entry points are checked by their observation specs and effect traces; their inputs are anchored, so no mapping is involved. Every changed kernel method pair that alignment matches is checked by the heap engine (spec::heap::check_with, new) under alignment's own proposal and the proof cache, held to its result, its exception and the identity of the result with each object parameter of its class. The report gives the obligations, what was reused, and the effort: a person's decisions in five categories, zero included, then the questions left and what nobody decided. lib/tests/compare.rs holds it to Phase 5's table on the fixture and its six defects, inline, in 15 s. Every row passes except exact reuse, which is partial: the kernel's rerun results are exact hits from the first run, but the entry points' effect checks are not cached yet. That is the next step, then examples 190-199.

Two disagreements between streams were reconciled. First, alignment proposed an output relation for a result whose class changed shape, which heap holds for a person's approval, although heap compares such a result itself under the equations of an input of the same class. Pricing#withQuantity was therefore unresolved under alignment's proposal but verified under the golden correspondence. Alignment now leaves the relation out when an input's equations say the same, term by term (tests/alignment.rs updated; Q#make, with no such input, keeps its relation). Second, heap's fixture note: the alias-to-copy copy threw for a quantity below 1, so the defect was refuted on the exception, not on result == q. The copy is now made for one item and then given the quantity; on a JVM, over 270 cases, every field agrees with after's and result == q never holds. Heap's two tests of that defect were updated to match. Also added: proof_cache::key_mark and key_since, so that a proposal's evidence names its claim key, and the fixture's compiler moved to lib/tests/foundations_fixture/, shared with tests/foundations.rs.

commits.summary: The entry points' effect-trace proofs under the proof cache: Phase 5's exact-reuse row passes, and the stale-cache defect is checked at the boundary
commits.body:
effects::check_with runs an entry point's effect-trace proof with equivalence's proof cache, from jvmcontract effects --cache DIR and from compare --cache. The proof is a regression check of the two builds rewritten with recording stubs, so its claim key digests their closures from the generated entry method: the stubs, and with them the environment model they encode (the modeled calls in order, the payload paths snapshotted, the trace bound, the exception classes, the string literals). What the result adds to the proof (the specs' unresolved parts, the external inputs, the status mapping) is worked out again on every run, and a stored refutation's witness is replayed on a JVM again. Each result records its claim key and any exact reuse.

Verified inline. tests/effects.rs has a new test, an_effect_proof_is_reused_exactly_when_its_claim_is_unchanged: a rerun is an exact hit. One more attempt allowed, a payload path no longer snapshotted, a @ResponseStatus added to the route (the status then unresolved) and a dropped event in the handler each miss under another key. A rerun of the dropped event reuses its stored refutation, replayed on a JVM with the same attempts. The Spring stand-in HttpStatus gained CREATED for it. In tests/compare.rs the joint run's rerun reuses POST /quotes's proof under the first run's key. The defects that POST /quotes reaches prove it again. alias-to-copy changes only a method the route doesn't reach, so it reuses the proof, rightly. Every row of Phase 5's table now passes. The fixture is not yet examples 190-199, which is next.

Full Rust suite: lib 203, alignment 34, compare 1, conformance 9 (2 ignored), effects 17, foundations 3, heap 46 (9 ignored), integration 64, observations 12, skill 1, summaries 40. In the full run, integration's the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs timed out under load (Engine::probe budgets by wall clock, a known note in the brief) and passed alone in 8 s. The brief's Progress records the cycle; the rest of the brief is unchanged and still right.

commits.summary: Examples 190-196: the joint example run by build.py through jvmcontract compare, on the new shop app; Phase 5 done (verification pending)
commits.body:
Phase 0 asked Phase 5 to make the joint example's fixture an example under the numbers 190-199. The new app examples/apps/shop is the fixture's before build, with Spring stand-ins and plain tests through the route; seven examples patch it into the fixture's after build (190, verified) and each defect overlaid on it: offset (191) and alias-to-copy (192) refuted in the kernel, dropped-effect (193) and duplicated-effect (194) refuted at the route, outside-domain (195) verified within the constructor-made domain, route-change (196) unresolved with four questions. A new technique tag, joint-run, groups them.

build.py gained run_tool_compare: jvmcontract compare twice under one fresh proof cache, the page from the first run and the verdict from the rerun's JSON, the verdict being the example's subject (an entry point's handler or a kernel method) and every other part recorded in the result's new joint field (verdict, exact hit on the rerun, proved helpers, obligations, decisions, questions, assumptions). jvmcontract compare gained --report DIR (with --sources and --base), writing compare.sarif with an effects-changed finding per refuted entry point and a behaviour-changed one per refuted kernel pair, since build.py records a violation only with a report.

Verified: jvmcontract compare inline on the app compiled unpatched and patched gives each example's expected verdict, every decided proof an exact hit on the rerun, and the SARIF findings anchored in the app's sources; the app's tests pass on every version but offset; six new mocked runner tests and the rest of test_build.py (179) pass; cargo tests lib 203, compare 1 (now checking the findings), effects 17, foundations 3 pass. build.py itself is not run inline on B9 examples: seven quick jobs, none yet run (no runner active), for review: 20261107-140010-example-190-through-build-py-the-joint-e, 20261107-140010-example-191-through-build-py-the-joint-e, 20261107-140010-example-192-through-build-py-the-joint-e, 20261107-140010-example-193-through-build-py-the-joint-e, 20261107-140010-example-194-through-build-py-the-joint-e, 20261107-140011-example-195-through-build-py-the-joint-e, 20261107-140011-example-196-through-build-py-the-joint-e.

The brief's Progress records this cycle and sets the status to done: every row of Phase 5's table passes, and what is left (heap's two fixture notes, the temporary paths a reuse names) is small and bears on no row.

commits.summary: Record verification results for 28 jobs: the foundations loop's pending jobs, 18 passed and 10 failed, triaged into VF-015 to VF-019
commits.body:
The 28 jobs the foundations loop left pending ran on vm-1 (12 workers). 18 passed: examples 170-172 and 190-196 with their expected verdicts, S6's proof-cache economics, Crosscut's nine examples rerun after the retry throttle, and five of the heap stream's H2/H5 tests under JBMC and auto --confirm. The alignment A3 scoring passed but one output had changed since its commit, so it is resubmitted unchanged as 20261107-155804-alignment-a3-second-half-every-proposal.

10 failed, recorded in verification/findings.md: VF-016, examples 160 and 161 stop in build.py because their subject is a caller the patch doesn't change; VF-017, examples 150-152 fail result validation because examples/schema/result.schema.json has no 'object' parameter kind (still so at main); VF-018, four H5 tests where JBMC doesn't finish within 600 s on proofs the own checker makes; VF-019, under auto --confirm H2's six nullable and may-alias claims give 'no engine wrote a harness' (job 20261107-043420, beside VF-009's 8 disagreements, seen again). VF-015 records example 109's 2026-11-03 failure, never tracked: its witness can't be replayed because the interpreter can't read StandardCharsets.UTF_8. Each entry is assigned to a stream of the cleanup loop, whose briefs follow in the next commit.

commits.summary: The cleanup loop's briefs: three streams that work through the open verification findings, with the pipeline
commits.body:
llm-dlc/loops/cleanup.md plans a loop that closes the open entries of verification/findings.md rather than adding features. Each entry is closed only by the check it names, by the /run-verification agent. Three streams run in parallel jj workspaces, forked from the planning session: native (the own checker: VF-010 probe budgets by solver work, not wall clock; VF-011 unwinding counted per loop entry; VF-015 example 109's replay), jbmc (VF-009 and VF-019 under auto --confirm, VF-001's remainder, VF-018 JBMC's timeouts on H5's object proofs) and examples (VF-002 and VF-016 in build.py's subject check, VF-017 the result schema's missing object kind, VF-014 H1's benchmark isolated against its parent with submit --revision, VF-013 publishing the loops' run records redacted, and the foundations leftovers). After the merge the main loop publishes the run records and reruns the merge's examples. Each item's facts were rechecked against main at tqwpwkvz.

The user settled seven decisions on 2026-11-07, recorded in the brief: external JBMC work stays deferred; VF-010 and VF-013 are in; the encoding-estimate flake stays known; three streams with the verification pipeline; VF-018 gets one rerun at an 1800 s limit, then is deferred to the user; and each stream runs in a 4 GB scope. A clean cargo test build of lib/ peaked at 3.1 GiB, so the launch command sets CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=8. feature-loop.sh and run-streams.sh know the names cleanup and cleanup-STREAM, and llm-dlc/tools/cleanup-integration.sh is the integration check (the library's unit, foundations, compare and effects tests, plus test_build.py, the benchmark's and sync.py's review tests). It passed on main in 85 s: 224 Rust tests and 234 Python tests. bash -n passes on both loop scripts.
Brings the published traces up to this point: conversation that came after a session's last commit, and sessions with no commit of their own.

commits.summary: run-streams.sh: workspaces named by each stream brief, the integration workspace by the brief, and taken directories refused before anything starts
commits.body:
The first launch of the cleanup loop stopped after adding its three stream workspaces. The integration workspace is added at ../REPO-integration, and the foundations run had left that directory behind when its workspace was forgotten, so jj workspace add failed. The planning session had already been compacted by then.

run-streams.sh now takes each stream's workspace from its brief's '- workspace:' setting, which must be unique among the streams and may not be default or NAME-integration. It no longer has to equal the stream's name, and it is used for the merge revisions and the heads. The integration workspace is NAME-integration (../REPO-NAME-integration), so briefs no longer share one. Before compacting the planning session, the script checks every directory it would add a workspace at. If one is already there, it names the directory and stops. The cleanup briefs use cleanup-native, cleanup-jbmc and cleanup-examples. The launch command spells out FEATURE_LOOP_MEMORY_MAX=4G, because shells started before ~/.profile changed still carry 8G, which overrides the briefs' memory setting. The three workspaces the failed start made (native, jbmc, examples, all empty) are forgotten in jj, and their directories are left for the user.

Tested in a throwaway jj repository, with stub claude and feature-loop.sh. A taken stream directory and a taken integration directory each stop the run before the compaction. With all directories free, the run adds cleanup-native, cleanup-jbmc, cleanup-examples and cleanup-integration, runs the three stream loops and the merge loop, and finishes. jj new on the three cleanup-STREAM@- revisions works in the integration workspace. bash -n passes.
